meta.description: US LNG export projects: operating, under construction, and FID'd, with nameplate feedgas-equivalent capacity and ramp timing through 2031. Built to model US LNG feedgas demand growth from ~15-16 Bcf/d nameplate (end-2025) toward ~30-35 Bcf/d by 2030-31.
meta.conversion_note: Capacity in Bcf/d = mtpa x 0.132 (approximate feedgas equivalent including liquefaction fuel/shrinkage). 'Nameplate' understates realized peak feedgas: Venture Global facilities and Sabine Pass/Freeport routinely run 10-25% above nameplate. US feedgas already exceeded 20 Bcf/d on peak winter 2025-26 days against ~15-16 Bcf/d nameplate.

status_definitions.operating: Producing LNG (at least first train), may still be ramping
status_definitions.under-construction: FID taken, construction underway, no LNG production yet from that phase/train
status_definitions.FID: Final investment decision taken 2025-2026, early construction
status_definitions.pre-FID-but-likely: Fully or nearly fully commercialized, FID expected but not yet taken as of July 2026

projects.name: Sabine Pass LNG (Trains 1-6)
projects.notes: Six trains. Observed peak feedgas ~4.5-5.0 Bcf/d, well above nameplate. Cheniere is developing a ~20 mtpa SPL Expansion (pre-FID, listed separately).

projects.name: Corpus Christi LNG (Trains 1-3)
projects.notes: Three large trains, ~5 mtpa each.

projects.name: Corpus Christi Stage 3 (midscale Trains 1-7)
projects.notes: First LNG Dec 2024. Trains 1-4 substantially complete in 2025; Train 5 complete Mar 2026, Train 6 first LNG Jun 2026, Train 7 substantial completion expected end-2026. With Stage 3 + Trains 8-9 + debottlenecking, total CCL capacity exceeds 30 mtpa later this decade.

projects.name: Corpus Christi Midscale Trains 8-9 + debottlenecking
projects.notes: FID June 2025, full NTP to Bechtel. Over 3 mtpa from two midscale trains plus debottlenecking.

projects.name: Freeport LNG (Trains 1-3)
projects.notes: Electric-drive trains; peak feedgas ~2.2-2.4 Bcf/d. Train 4 remains pre-FID (not counted).

projects.name: Cameron LNG (Trains 1-3)
projects.notes: Phase 2 (Train 4) deferred/pre-FID, not counted.

projects.name: Cove Point LNG
projects.notes: Single train.

projects.name: Elba Island LNG
projects.notes: Ten small modular units. DOE approved ~0.1 Bcf/d additional export volume in 2026.

projects.name: Calcasieu Pass LNG
projects.notes: First LNG Jan 2022; formal COD April 2025 after long commissioning. Runs well above nameplate (peak ~12.4 mtpa).

projects.name: Plaquemines LNG Phase 1
projects.notes: FID Mar 2022. First LNG Dec 2024. 18 midscale trains in phase. All Phase 1 facilities expected in service Q4 2026. Per-phase nominal output 1.3 Bcf/d, peak 1.6 Bcf/d.

projects.name: Plaquemines LNG Phase 2
projects.notes: FID Mar 2023. Shipping cargoes; remaining Phase 2 facilities in service by mid-2027. Combined Plaquemines nameplate 20 mtpa, peak 27.2 mtpa (~3.2 Bcf/d output); feedgas already averaged >3 Bcf/d in 2026.

projects.name: Golden Pass LNG Train 1
projects.notes: First LNG Mar 30, 2026; first cargo Apr 22, 2026, after Chapter 11 EPC reset delays.

projects.name: Golden Pass LNG Train 2
projects.notes: EIA expects Trains 1-2 (combined ~1.4 Bcf/d) in service during 2026.

projects.name: Golden Pass LNG Train 3
projects.notes: EIA expects Train 3 (~0.7 Bcf/d) to begin exports in 2027. Total facility ~18 mtpa.

projects.name: Port Arthur LNG Phase 1 (Trains 1-2)
projects.notes: FID Mar 2023. Train 1 COD expected 2027, Train 2 2028. EIA carries Phase 1 at 1.6 Bcf/d.

projects.name: Port Arthur LNG Phase 2 (Trains 3-4)
projects.notes: FID Sept 22, 2025 (~$14B). COD Train 3 in 2030, Train 4 in 2031. 10 mtpa contracted to ConocoPhillips, JERA, EQT.

projects.name: Rio Grande LNG Phase 1 (Trains 1-3)
projects.notes: FID Jul 2023. Brownsville. Train 1 first LNG expected 2027 (EIA has Trains 1-2, 1.4 Bcf/d, beginning exports 2027); Train 3 into 2028-29.

projects.name: Rio Grande LNG Train 4
projects.notes: FID and financial close Sept 9, 2025 (~0.9 Bcf/d per RBN).

projects.name: Rio Grande LNG Train 5
projects.notes: FID and financial close Oct 16, 2025 (~$6.7B). Guaranteed substantial completion / first commercial delivery H1 2031; first LNG likely 2030.

projects.name: CP2 LNG Phase 1
projects.notes: FID/financial close Jul 2025. First LNG expected H2 2027 — fastest FID-to-first-LNG for a large-scale project. Full CP2 nameplate 20 mtpa, peak ~28-29 mtpa; EIA carries Phase 1 at 2.0 Bcf/d.

projects.name: CP2 LNG Phase 2
projects.notes: FID and $8.6B financial close Mar 2026. Nameplate 5.6 mtpa, expected peak ~8 mtpa.

projects.name: Louisiana LNG (Trains 1-3, ex-Driftwood)
projects.notes: FID Apr 2025 (~$17.5B). Three trains; foundation phase ~22% complete mid-2026; first LNG targeted 2029. EIA carries at 2.2 Bcf/d.

projects.name: Commonwealth LNG
projects.notes: FID May 15, 2026 (~$12.5-13B). Modular design at Cameron, LA. Sources cite 9.5 mtpa peak / ~8.4 mtpa nameplate; first production targeted 2030.

projects.name: Delfin FLNG 1
projects.notes: FID Jun 3, 2026 — first US floating LNG FID. 4.4 mtpa per FID announcements (earlier guidance ~3-3.5 mtpa/vessel); up to 4 vessels (13.3 mtpa) ultimately. Production expected 2030.

projects.name: Texas LNG
projects.notes: Brownsville. Fully subscribed offtake; $500M BlackRock-affiliate investment; limited NTP to Kiewit issued early Jul 2026; FID targeted 2026. Not counted in aggregate ramp.

projects.name: Plaquemines Expansion (Phase 1 of 3)
projects.notes: FERC application filed 2025 for 32 modular trains adding >30 mtpa peak across three phases; FID targeted ~2027. Capacity shown is approximate first-phase share. Not counted in aggregate ramp.

projects.name: Sabine Pass Expansion (SPL Stage 5)
projects.notes: ~20 mtpa expansion in FERC pre-filing/permitting; FID likely 2026-2027, first LNG ~2030s. Not counted in aggregate ramp.

projects.name: Lake Charles LNG
projects.notes: FID plans suspended mid-Dec 2025 as Energy Transfer refocused on pipelines; heavily commercialized, could revive. Weakest of the pre-FID group. Not counted in aggregate ramp.

aggregate_ramp.description: Best-estimate cumulative US nameplate LNG feedgas demand (Bcf/d) at each year-end, operating + under-construction + FID'd projects only (pre-FID excluded). Nameplate basis = mtpa x 0.132; realized peak feedgas runs ~10-20% higher (winter 2025-26 already saw >20 Bcf/d days).

drivers_by_year.2026: CC Stage 3 Trains 5-7, Golden Pass Trains 1-2, Plaquemines Phase 1 full in-service
drivers_by_year.2027: Golden Pass Train 3, Port Arthur Train 1, Rio Grande Train 1, CP2 Phase 1 first LNG (partial), Plaquemines Phase 2 full in-service
drivers_by_year.2028: Port Arthur Train 2, Rio Grande Train 2, CP2 Phase 1 ramp, CC Midscale Trains 8-9
drivers_by_year.2029: Rio Grande Train 3, CP2 Phase 2 first LNG, Louisiana LNG Train 1
drivers_by_year.2030: Louisiana LNG Trains 2-3, Port Arthur Train 3, Rio Grande Train 4, Commonwealth first LNG, Delfin FLNG 1
drivers_by_year.2031: Port Arthur Train 4, Rio Grande Train 5, Commonwealth full ramp

aggregate_ramp.upside_note: Pre-FID-but-likely projects (Texas LNG, Plaquemines Expansion, Sabine Pass Expansion, Lake Charles) could add ~0.5-1.5 Bcf/d by 2031 and far more post-2031. EIA (Apr 2026) forecasts LNG export volumes of 17.0 Bcf/d in 2026 and 18.5 Bcf/d in 2027; EIA counts ~13.9 Bcf/d of capacity additions 2025-2029 taking North America to 28.7 Bcf/d by 2029. Independent forecasts (Enverus) put US feedgas at ~33 Bcf/d by 2030.
